name: Jobs that do not conflict run side by side
summary: A job declares the resources it holds - the phone, a repository, the build machine; jobs that share none run in parallel, so work goes on while a phone reboots or a kernel builds.
why: Waiting is shrunk best by not waiting at all.

name: Waits are measured where they happen
summary: Every submit --wait and every wait records itself: what was waited on (a build, a reboot, CI, a harvest), for which project, how long. Gathered into each project's data like commits - made by the work, never typed.
why: The author: waiting is a chore of its own, and grows as more is automated; it must be seen to be shrunk.
